instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Thirty-one, a bit-part signing at Southampton and two years past his City peak; the movement had gone.
Still a utility player filling in across the back and midfield in his first season; the athleticism was obvious, the centre-back was not yet.
A converted midfielder who was an unbeaten side’s first-choice centre-back at 22; pace and recovery already elite.
Arguably the best goalkeeper outside the top four in this season; shot-stopping close to elite, sits with Flowers (81) rather than Seaman (86).
Dropped for Carroll after the Porto error; the ability had not changed much but the season was a fragmented one.
A Euro 96 winner and a Bayern and Milan left wing-back; six goals and six assists for a lower-half side, and comfortably the best player in it.
A treble-winning squad, but injury and Carragher restricted him to eleven starts; rated below his Middlesbrough season on form, not on standing.
A 52-cap Germany international, but at 30 in his final season and physically finished; rated well below his Stuttgart peak.

Rated for the ability, not the outcome: a genuinely exceptional dribbler and the one player in a relegated City side who would have started for most of the division. Held under 80 because the end product was slight.
Persistent foot and hamstring injuries from 1994 effectively ended him as a top-level full-back; five starts in two seasons and a clear drop from the England regular of 1993/94.
Went from fringe to a regular in a title-winning back four at 21; comfortable on either flank and rarely exposed.
Returned to Oldham in a swap deal early in 1993/94.
A combative but technically sound midfielder who went on to a French title and a Roma career; one of Everton’s better players that season.
His best English season: a first-choice midfielder in a Champions League semi-final side and the one who made it function defensively.
Scored the goal that won the title at Old Trafford in a double season; a France starter at his peak.
A France international and European champion used as a rotation forward at 29; still a quality top-four attacker rather than a squad filler.
An undemonstrative but excellent screening midfielder and a World Cup winner; a clear starter in an all-time great side.
A stress fracture in the back cost him most of the second half of the season; rated on the player, not the availability.
World class: pace, strength and reading combined, and in 1998/99 in the conversation for the best centre-back in Europe. Rated above Adams (88) and just under Ferdinand 2007/08 (91).
An Achilles rupture cost him the first half of the season and he was sold that summer; still world class when he played, a point off his peak.
